--- title: "Diagnostics & Calibration" description: "Understand and improve your predictions — uncertainty decomposition, PIT diagnostics, recalibration, and SHAP attribution" date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- # Diagnostics & Calibration A model with 90% nominal coverage that actually achieves 85% is **miscalibrated**. This notebook shows how to: 1. **Decompose uncertainty** into aleatoric (data noise) vs epistemic (model) components 2. **Diagnose calibration** with PIT histograms and reliability diagrams 3. **Identify uncertainty drivers** — which features make predictions uncertain 4. **Recalibrate** miscalibrated models with isotonic regression 5. **Attribute interval width** to features via SHAP ## Setup ::: {#setup .cell cache='true' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor from uncertainty_flow import ( ConformalRegressor, coverage_score, winkler_score, pinball_loss, EnsembleDecomposition, ) from uncertainty_flow.utils import select_validation_plan from uncertainty_flow.calibration import RecalibratedModel from uncertainty_flow.calibration.residual_analysis import compute_uncertainty_drivers ``` ::: ::: {#data-load .cell cache='true' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pl.read_parquet("../data/concrete.parquet") plan = select_validation_plan(df, task_type="tabular") train_df, test_df = plan.outer_split print(f"Train: {len(train_df)} Test: {len(test_df)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Train: 824 Test: 206 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#fit-model .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} model = ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), coverage_target=0.9, ) model.fit(train_df, target="strength") pred = model.predict(test_df) y_true = test_df["strength"] ``` ::: ## Uncertainty Decomposition ### Lightweight Heuristic `pred.uncertainty_decomposition()` gives a cheap per-prediction estimate without refitting: ::: {#heuristic-decomposition .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} decomp = pred.uncertainty_decomposition() print(f"Total: {decomp['total']:.2f}") print(f" Aleatoric (data noise): {decomp['aleatoric']:.2f}") print(f" Epistemic (model): {decomp['epistemic']:.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Total: 22.30 Aleatoric (data noise): 22.30 Epistemic (model): 0.00 ``` ::: ::: ### Bootstrap Ensemble Decomposition `EnsembleDecomposition` refits the model on bootstrap resamples for a principled decomposition: ::: {#ensemble-decomposition .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} ensemble = EnsembleDecomposition( model_factory=lambda: ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), coverage_target=0.9, ), train_data=train_df, target="strength", n_bootstrap=15, random_state=42, ) decomp_ens = ensemble.decompose(test_df) print(f"Ensemble — Total: {decomp_ens['total']:.2f}") print(f" Aleatoric: {decomp_ens['aleatoric']:.2f}") print(f" Epistemic: {decomp_ens['epistemic']:.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` /Users/minghao/Desktop/personal/uncertainty_flow/uncertainty_flow/wrappers/conformal.py:237: UncertaintyFlowWarning: Residual correlation analysis found no significant drivers. A U-shaped histogram means intervals are too narrow; a hump means too wide. ::: {#cell-pit-histogram .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} pred.plot_pit(y_true) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](03_diagnostics_calibration_files/figure-html/pit-histogram-output-1.png){#pit-histogram width=758 height=470} ::: ::: ### Calibration Curve (Reliability Diagram) Compares expected (nominal) coverage to observed (empirical) coverage: ::: {#cell-calibration-curve .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} cal = pred.calibration_curve(y_true, n_bins=20) expected = cal["expected_coverage"].to_numpy() observed = cal["observed_coverage"].to_numpy() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 7)) ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "k--", alpha=0.5, label="Perfect calibration") ax.plot(expected, observed, "o-", color="#4C78A8", markersize=4, label="Model") ax.set_xlabel("Expected coverage") ax.set_ylabel("Observed coverage") ax.set_title("Reliability Diagram") ax.legend() ax.set_aspect("equal") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](03_diagnostics_calibration_files/figure-html/calibration-curve-output-1.png){#calibration-curve width=651 height=662} ::: ::: ### Calibration Report ::: {#calibration-report .cell We use a separate calibration split: ::: {#cell-recalibration-setup .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} plan_3way = select_validation_plan(df, task_type="tabular") train_all, holdout = plan_3way.outer_split plan_inner = select_validation_plan(train_all, task_type="tabular") train_sub, calib_sub = plan_inner.outer_split model_base = ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), coverage_target=0.9, ) model_base.fit(train_sub, target="strength") ``` ::: {#recalibration-setup .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ``` ``` ::: ::: ::: {#recalibrate .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} recal = RecalibratedModel(model=model_base) recal.fit(calib_sub, target="strength") pred_recal = recal.predict(holdout) y_hold = holdout["strength"] ``` ::: ### Before vs After ::: {#before-after-metrics .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} pred_before = model_base.predict(holdout) int_before = pred_before.interval(0.9) int_after = pred_recal.interval(0.9) print("Before Recalibration:") print(f" Coverage: {coverage_score(y_hold, int_before['lower'], int_before['upper']):.4f}") print(f" Winkler: {winkler_score(y_hold, int_before['lower'], int_before['upper'], 0.9):.2f}") print("After Recalibration:") print(f" Coverage: {coverage_score(y_hold, int_after['lower'], int_after['upper']):.4f}") print(f" Winkler: {winkler_score(y_hold, int_after['lower'], int_after['upper'], 0.9):.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Before Recalibration: Coverage: 0.7427 Winkler: 54.35 After Recalibration: Coverage: 0.6117 Winkler: 61.15 ``` ::: ::: ### PIT Comparison ::: {#cell-pit-comparison .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5)) for ax, p, title in [ (axes[0], pred_before, "Before Recalibration"), (axes[1], pred_recal, "After Recalibration"), ]: hist = p.pit_histogram(y_hold, n_bins=10) centers = hist["bin_center"].to_numpy() counts = hist["count"].to_numpy() expected = hist["expected"].to_numpy() width = centers[1] - centers[0] if len(centers) > 1 else 0.1 ax.bar(centers, counts, width=width * 0.9, alpha=0.7, color="#4C78A8", label="PIT counts") ax.axhline(y=expected[0], color="red", linestyle="--", label="Uniform reference") ax.set_xlabel("PIT value") ax.set_ylabel("Count") ax.set_title(title) ax.legend() plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](03_diagnostics_calibration_files/figure-html/pit-comparison-output-1.png){#pit-comparison width=1142 height=470} ::: ::: ## SHAP: What Drives Interval Width? ::: {#shap .cell execution_count=18} ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Key Takeaways | Diagnostic | What it tells you | |------------|-------------------| | `pred.uncertainty_decomposition()` | Quick aleatoric vs epistemic split (no refitting) | | `EnsembleDecomposition` | Principled decomposition via bootstrap refits | | `pred.plot_pit(y_true)` | Calibration check: flat = good | | `pred.calibration_curve(y_true)` | Reliability diagram | | `compute_uncertainty_drivers()` | Which features drive heteroscedasticity | | `RecalibratedModel` | Fix miscalibration with isotonic regression | | `uncertainty_shap()` | Feature attribution for interval width |
